scope: Bounded comparison of the WPF cashier refund submission/HTTP result path and the WinUI cashier refund submission/recovery path, shared refund API endpoint/server idempotency, unique persistence key, and checked-in same-key refund integration tests. Does not assert WPF deployment or execute tests.
decision: The client refund flows differ in how they handle uncertain outcomes. WPF creates a fresh RefundRequestId on every SubmitRefundAsync invocation and its ApiClient posts then parses a response without converting transport exceptions into an OutcomeUnknown result; the ViewModel has no retained pending request. WinUI retains _pendingRefund and retries the same request object/ID after a reported unknown outcome during the current ViewModel lifetime, and only rotates _refundRequestId after success. The server derives refund-{RefundRequestId}, replays by that key, and has a unique OrderRefund.IdempotencyKey index. Therefore an operator-initiated WPF retry after an ambiguous transport outcome is a new server command; it is not same-key replay. Because the order lock, refundable remainder clamp, and protected source-account balance still apply, this does not establish over-refund or cash loss. A second partial refund may nevertheless be a distinct additional refund if the first was accepted and the operator submits again without first reconciling. WinUI’s pending request is memory-only, so process/session loss can also discard the same-key recovery context. WPF project inclusion is source-confirmed; deployment/use is unknown.
finding_candidate: Conditional client recovery divergence; no canonical financial defect assigned pending independent challenge and WPF deployment/policy confirmation.

manual_reasoning.WPF_path: SubmitRefundAsync creates rreq-{Guid.NewGuid()} on each command invocation, parses amount via decimal.TryParse and Math.Round, sends one RefundAsync request, reports returned error, and refreshes order only on success. Its IsRefunding flag is reset in finally. There is no retained pending request/id or explicit unknown-outcome state in the cited ViewModel. WPF ApiClient RefundAsync posts directly and calls ReadResultAsync; ReadResultAsync maps HTTP statuses but does not catch transport exceptions or expose OutcomeUnknown.
manual_reasoning.WinUI_path: SubmitRefundAsync either builds a request with persistent _refundRequestId or reuses _pendingRefund; CompleteRefundAsync stores the request before sending and retains it when the outcome is unknown, rotates ID after success, and updates local refund state from server result. ApiClient.SendAsync turns transport/serialization failures into OutcomeUnknown with same-data retry guidance. The pending request itself is in-memory only; restart persistence is not established.
manual_reasoning.server_boundary: RefundOrderHandler maps RefundRequestId to refund-{id}, looks up prior receipt, then locks the order, clamps requested amount to remaining refundable, protects the selected treasury source balance, writes order refund + treasury movement + audit in one transaction, and handles constrained conflicts by replay lookup. FalahDbContext configures a unique OrderRefund IdempotencyKey index. Distinct request IDs are distinct commands, not replays.
manual_reasoning.tests: Checked-in RefundVerticalSliceTests asserts sequential and concurrent same-ID requests produce one refund/movement, and distinct-ID concurrent requests do not exceed order total. Test source was inspected only; no tests executed. It does not test client transport ambiguity, WPF retry UX, or WinUI process restart recovery.
manual_reasoning.behavior_classification: Client semantic divergence and retry-recovery gap conditional on WPF use; not a demonstrated duplicate payout, over-refund, or server idempotency defect. Separate from FIN-CAND-REFUND-REPLAY-001, which concerns server same-key overlapping full refund ordering.

recommendation.classification: Conditional LOW client reliability/policy concern; deployment and desired legacy-client support unknown.
recommendation.action: If WPF remains a supported cashier, route command calls through an explicit unknown-outcome result and retain/reconcile the original refund request ID before allowing a new refund attempt. If WPF is retired, record that deployment fact and avoid unnecessary legacy repair. For WinUI, decide whether unresolved operation recovery must survive application restart; if yes, persist a safe pending operation identifier/data or require server-side order/refund reconciliation before issuing a new request. Do not change shared server amount/account guards.
required_tests: WPF transport exception after server acceptance: operator retry must reuse the same request ID or require authoritative order/refund reconciliation before a new command.
WinUI timeout/response-loss followed by retry uses identical request ID and yields one saved refund; app restart behavior follows documented owner policy.
New, intentional partial refund with a new operation ID remains allowed and independently auditable.
Same-key sequential/concurrent and distinct-key concurrent server tests continue proving replay and cumulative amount limits.
acceptance: Owner states whether WPF cashier is supported/deployed.
Ambiguous results cannot silently encourage a fresh refund command before reconciling the prior operation.
Repeated same logical operation uses stable idempotency key across retries.
Legitimate new partial refunds remain possible under explicit user intent and server limits.
counterevidence: WPF is a source project but active deployment is unknown; current active cashier has elsewhere been identified as WinUI.
Server clamps to refundable remaining and protects account balance, so source does not show over-refund or negative treasury.
Same-ID server replay is covered by checked-in integration-test source.
WinUI pending state is not shown as durable across process restart.
limitations: No transport fault injection, runtime/API/SQL test, or financial transaction executed.
No evidence that the UI auto-retries; concern is a manual new submit after ambiguity.

reviewer: Main coordinator comparison; independently challenged by financial_integrity_continuation; source-only.

independent_challenge.conclusion: WPF SubmitRefundAsync creates rreq-{Guid.NewGuid()} for each invocation, invokes RefundAsync once, and resets IsRefunding in finally. WPF ApiClient posts and parses HTTP results but has no transport-exception-to-OutcomeUnknown conversion. WinUI builds a request only when _pendingRefund is null; CompleteRefundAsync stores it before send, retains it for OutcomeUnknown, and reuses it on the next submit. It rotates the ID only after success. This is an in-memory recovery context; durability across process restart is not established by these files. A manual WPF re-submit after an ambiguous transport exception is a distinct idempotency command. If a prior partial refund committed, the second command may be another separately recorded refund, subject to the remaining-refund clamp and authorization. This is not evidence of an automatic retry, duplicate posting under one key, over-refund, or cash/account loss. Server locks the order and checks the protected source balance before recording the refund. A full already-refunded order has no positive remainder and is rejected. Disposition: Corroborate the source-described client difference and conditional recovery concern. Keep severity conditional/low; do not classify as duplicate-payment/over-refund or merge with FIN-CAND-REFUND-REPLAY-001. The latter remains a separate server replay-result edge, not evidence of multiple movement postings.
